# Analyst evidence package

This directory contains flat JSONL sample tuples for 338 same-task bad/good
AgentReward pairs drawn from 440 source trajectories. The semantic stack is
`task -> subtask -> strategy -> action -> object -> result`.

Each line in `samples.jsonl` has exactly these fields:

- `sample_type`: pprof sample type;
- `unit`: pprof sample unit;
- `value`: signed sample value, with positive for the bad side and negative
  for the good side;
- `stack_frames`: ordered pprof frame names in leaf-to-root order; and
- `labels`: the exact pprof string labels, represented as key-to-value-list.

The file preserves duplicate tuples and source order. It contains no derived
rates, pair manifest, aggregate result summary, or rendered figure.

Basic inspection examples:

```bash
head -n 1 samples.jsonl | jq .
jq -c 'select(.value > 0)' samples.jsonl
jq -c 'select(.value < 0)' samples.jsonl
```

item.text: {"diagnosis":"Candidate/bad runs overrepresent repeated actions: 1,485 repeated operations versus 224 in base/good runs. Repetition comprises 20.2% of bad operations but only 5.9% of good operations (3.40×), especially repeated clicks, no-ops, and scrolling.","expected_mechanism":"Detecting unchanged outcomes and forcing a strategy change interrupts unproductive loops, improving task progress and reducing wasted actions. The cost is state comparison, retry bookkeeping, and occasional premature abandonment of a retry that might eventually succeed.","policy_text":"Track each action’s observable outcome. If the same or materially equivalent action produces no state change twice, do not repeat it unchanged: inspect the state, alter the target or strategy, or stop that branch. Permit another retry only when new evidence makes success more likely.","quantitative_evidence":[{"command":"jq -s 'def stats: {operations:(map(.value)|add), tuples:length, sessions:(map(.labels.source_session[0])|unique|length)}; {repeated_bad:(map(select(.stack_frames[0]==\"result:repeated\" and .value>0))|stats), repeated_good:(map(select(.stack_frames[0]==\"result:repeated\" and .value<0)|.value=-.value)|stats), all_bad:(map(select(.value>0))|stats), all_good:(map(select(.value<0)|.value=-.value)|stats)}' samples.jsonl","finding":"Repeated operations: bad=1,485 across 88 sessions; good=224 across 20 sessions. All operations: bad=7,366; good=3,780. Thus repeated-operation shares are 20.16% and 5.93%, respectively, a 3.40× relative overrepresentation."},{"command":"jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[0]==\"result:repeated\") | [.stack_frames[2],.value] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\\t' '{if($2>0)p[$1]+=$2; else n[$1]-=$2} END {for(k in p) printf \"%s\\tbad=%d\\tgood=%d\\texcess=%d\\n\",k,p[k],n[k],p[k]-n[k]}' | sort -t= -k4,4nr","finding":"Largest repeated-action excesses were click: 679 bad versus 40 good (+639); noop: 441 versus 85 (+356); and scroll: 278 versus 1 (+277)."}]}
